name: Monster Trainer Monster Breeder
body:
Monster breeders are able to change the very nature of their companions through the process of monster growth. By sacrificing some of the versatility given to other trainers, breeders can instead call upon more focused and powerful monsters over time.

Optional: Breeder Templates

In addition to advanced monster growth, a monster breeder can apply templates to his monsters to increase their CR (up to his monster trainer level). Given the varying strengths of many templates, this is a potentially powerful option, but it does add flavor to the archetype and gives access to a piece of the Pathfinder® Roleplaying Game not often utilized by players. Most breeders will use this option to apply simple templates, but if one wishes to seek out more complex templates, the GM has a few options for how to provide them.

Many breeders keep journals of the different templates they’ve encountered. Finding one of these journals is equivalent to finding a book of magic spells. There are some exotic merchants and hidden treasure troves with scrolls describing techniques that will apply a template to a single monster. These scrolls are often valued at the Template’s CR adjustment squared x 2,000 gp.

Some breeders are able to blend the essence of their monsters to produce new companions entirely. Doing so requires a monster that has similar properties to the template the breeder wishes to apply. For example, the breeder can apply the white half-dragon template to his monsters once he captures a white dragon or half-dragon.

Breeder’s Companion

Monster breeders form a stronger connection with their starting monsters than other trainers, and often keep those monsters in top condition. At 1st level, a monster breeder chooses animal companion, beloved monster, or familiar bond and gains that trainer perk. The breeder’s effective level with the chosen perk is equal to his full monster trainer level.

A breeder’s companion never counts as an active monster for the purpose of monster training, so the breeder can control an active monster while his companion acts independently. The companion cannot grant the breeder spells unless he also has the Monstrous Bond feat.

This ability alters the monster normally given to a trainer at 1st level and replaces eschew materials, the trainer perk gained at 4th level, and channel monster.

Advanced Monster Growth

At 2nd level, a monster breeder’s active monster always treats its base attack bonus as the breeder’s monster trainer level unless its own is higher, and it adds the breeder’s Charisma modifier as a morale bonus to the damage it deals with attacks. This otherwise functions as the beloved monster trainer perk.

Beginning at 9th level, the breeder’s active monster also adds the breeder’s Charisma bonus on all saving throws.

This ability replaces favored enemy and great trainer.
